name: Battle of Marathon
note: Persian landing beach. Marsh at both ends narrowed the front to ground the Athenians could hold.

name: Battle of Thermopylae
where: the strip between cliff and sea
note: THE SEA IS SIX KILOMETRES NORTH OF HERE NOW. The pass is in the terrain; the narrowness was made of water.

name: Battle of Salamis
where: the strait between the island and the shore
note: A sea-fight has no single position. This is the middle of the channel the Persian fleet entered.

name: Landing on Psyttaleia
where: the island in the channel mouth
note: Aristides put hoplites ashore on the island the Persians had garrisoned.

name: Athens burned by the Persians
note: The Older Parthenon was destroyed. Its burnt drums were built into the north wall and left visible.

name: Battle of Plataea
note: The last land battle of the Persian invasion, fought on the Boeotian plain under the pass.

name: The Themistoclean wall raised
note: Built in haste from whatever stood, including grave stelai — which is why the Kerameikos is dated by them.

name: The Long Walls begun
where: between the city and its port
note: Six miles of wall joining Athens to Piraeus, making the city an island as long as the fleet held.

name: The Parthenon begun
note: Built over the burnt foundations of its predecessor, thirty-three years after the Persians left.

name: The Peloponnesian War begins
note: Voted for on the Pnyx. The countryside was abandoned and the population brought inside the Long Walls.

name: The plague at Athens
where: the port and the crowded city
note: It came ashore at Piraeus and spread through a population packed inside the walls by the war.

name: Battle of Delion
note: An Athenian defeat in Boeotia. Sokrates is said to have retreated in good order.

name: The fleet sails for Sicily
note: A DEPARTURE, NOT A ROUTE. Where the fleet left from is recorded; the passage it took is not.

name: Sparta fortifies Dekeleia
note: A permanent garrison in sight of Athens. The silver mines stopped and the countryside was lost.

name: Battle of Arginusae aftermath
note: The generals were tried and executed for failing to recover the dead. Sokrates alone refused to put it to the vote.

name: The Long Walls pulled down
where: between the city and its port
note: Sparta required their demolition. The city and the port were separated again.

name: The return from Phyle
note: Thrasyboulos held the fort above the plain and marched down through Piraeus to end the Thirty.

name: The trial of Sokrates
where: the law courts on the Agora
note: Tried and condemned in the marketplace he had spent his life arguing in.

name: Plato founds the Academy
where: the olive grove outside the walls
note: A public gymnasion with shade and water, a mile from the city — not a retreat but a place anyone could reach.

name: Battle of Leuktra
note: Thebes broke the Spartan line and with it the reputation of Spartan infantry.

name: Battle of Chaeronea
note: Philip and Alexander ended the independence of the Greek cities on flat ground below the road north.

name: Aristotle founds the Lyceum
where: the gymnasion east of the city
note: The other school, on the far side of Athens from the Academy. Two of them in one small city.

name: Sulla storms Athens
note: The Roman assault came in at the weakest stretch of wall, by the potters' quarter and the graves.

name: The Herulian sack
where: the Agora and the lower city
note: Afterwards a new wall was thrown up enclosing a fraction of the old city, using the rubble of the Agora.

name: The Parthenon explodes
note: A Venetian shell reached the Ottoman powder store inside the temple. It had stood two thousand years.

name: The first modern Olympics
note: Held in the Panathenaic Stadium, which is a natural ravine adapted rather than a building.
